lessons.title: Introduce close family members
lessons.subtitle: Introduce close family members
lessons.outcome: Introduce close family members or a partner and say how they are related to you.

vocabulary.note: Singular family takes a singular verb.
Feminine. Say ma mère for my mother; mère is neutral, while maman is familiar.
Masculine. Say mon père for my father; papa is familiar.
Plural of un parent in the mother/father sense; a mixed group uses masculine plural. Not the general English word relatives.
Masculine. In fils meaning son, pronounce the final s; the l is silent. Plural les fils has the same spelling.
Feminine. Fille also means girl; ma fille here identifies a family relationship.
Masculine. Here a romantic partner, not a travelling companion. This everyday introduction does not specify legal marital status.
Feminine counterpart of compagnon in a romantic relationship. This everyday introduction does not specify legal marital status.

vocabulary.meaning: here is / here are; this is (introducing someone)
vocabulary.note: Use voici directly before the person or people you are introducing. It does not change for plural people.

dialogue.target: Bonjour, voici ma famille. Voici ma mère, Anne, et mon père, Paul.
dialogue.meaning: Hello, this is my family. This is my mother, Anne, and my father, Paul.

dialogue.target: Vos parents habitent ici ?
dialogue.meaning: Do your parents live here?

dialogue.target: Non, mes parents habitent à Lille. Voici mon compagnon, Karim, mon fils, Hugo, et ma fille, Zoé.
dialogue.meaning: No, my parents live in Lille. This is my partner, Karim, my son, Hugo, and my daughter, Zoé.

dialogue.target: Enchantée. Ma compagne, Alice, arrive demain.
dialogue.meaning: Pleased to meet you. My partner, Alice, arrives tomorrow.

grammar.title: Optional: my family, your family
grammar.explanation: Mon goes with a masculine singular noun (mon père, mon fils, mon compagnon); ma with a feminine singular noun (ma mère, ma fille, ma compagne); mes with a plural noun (mes parents). The possessive agrees with the family noun, not the person speaking. Use votre/vos when addressing an adult neighbour with vous. Voici ma fille introduces a daughter; une fille can also mean a girl. Choose the family members that fit your situation; the example is one fictional family.

sentenceActivity.prompt: Build: “This is my mother and my father.”
answers: Voici ma mère et mon père.
Voici mon père et ma mère.
sentenceActivity.hint: Start Voici; link the two people with et.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Keep ma with mère and mon with père. Either order introduces both people. Do not use mon mère or ma père.

lessons.title: Choose an item by colour
lessons.subtitle: Choose an item by colour
lessons.outcome: Name common colours and ask for a different colour while choosing clothes.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais ce pantalon en noir.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like these trousers in black.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: noir, noire, noirs, noires.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez ce pull en bleu ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have this jumper in blue?
vocabulary.note: Adjective: bleu, bleue, bleus, bleues.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for a red jacket.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: rouge for masculine or feminine singular; rouges in the plural.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez ce pull en vert ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have this jumper in green?
vocabulary.note: Adjective: vert, verte, verts, vertes. In en vert, keep the base colour form.
Adjective: jaune for masculine or feminine singular; jaunes in the plural.
Adjective: blanc, blanche, blancs, blanches. Notice the feminine blanche.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will take the grey trousers.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: gris, grise, gris, grises. Masculine plural keeps the same written form.
Colour adjective: rose for singular; roses for plural. Here a colour, not a flower.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for an orange scarf.
vocabulary.note: As a simple colour adjective, orange is invariable: une veste orange, des vestes orange. Here the colour, not the fruit.
As a simple colour adjective, marron is invariable: un pull marron, des chaussures marron. Here the colour, not a chestnut.

dialogue.target: Bonjour, vous avez cette veste en vert ou en bleu ?
dialogue.meaning: Hello, do you have this jacket in green or blue?

dialogue.target: Oui, en vert, en bleu et en noir. Il y a aussi une veste rouge.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, in green, blue and black. There is also a red jacket.

dialogue.target: Je prends la veste verte et la chemise blanche.
dialogue.meaning: I will take the green jacket and the white shirt.

dialogue.target: Et pour le tee-shirt : jaune, gris, rose, orange ou marron ?
dialogue.meaning: And for the T-shirt: yellow, grey, pink, orange or brown?

dialogue.target: Le tee-shirt jaune, s’il vous plaît.
dialogue.meaning: The yellow T-shirt, please.

grammar.title: Optional: colour after the noun
grammar.explanation: A simple colour usually follows its noun: une veste verte, un pantalon gris. Most colour adjectives agree with the noun: blanc becomes blanche, and rose becomes roses in the plural. Orange and marron stay unchanged as simple colour adjectives: des chaussures marron. En + base colour asks for a colour option: vous avez ce pull en vert ? Reuse noir and bleu from the existing shopping bank; they are not new senses.

sentenceActivity.prompt: Build: “I am looking for a red jacket.”
sentenceActivity.hint: Start Je cherche, then the item, then its colour.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Rouge follows veste and has the same singular form for a masculine or feminine noun. Une rouge veste is not the neutral beginner pattern here.

lessons.title: Say where something hurts
lessons.subtitle: Say where something hurts
lessons.outcome: Name a body location and use avoir mal with au, à la, à l’ or aux to say where it hurts.

vocabulary.meaning: to be in pain / to hurt
vocabulary.note: Use avoir mal à plus the body part. This is a language pattern, not a diagnosis.
À la stays separate.
Everyday word for the abdominal area.
The final s is silent.
Masculine. À + le becomes au. Final s is silent; le bras and les bras have the same noun spelling.
Feminine. Keep à la as two words.
Masculine. À + le becomes au. The final d is silent.
Feminine despite the ending. Keep à la as two words.
Feminine: une oreille. La elides to l’ before the vowel; retain à before l’.
Feminine plural; singular une dent. À + les becomes aux. This body noun extends the existing se brosser les dents action target.

dialogue.target: Bonjour. Vous avez mal où ?
dialogue.meaning: Hello. Where does it hurt?

dialogue.target: J’ai mal à l’oreille.
dialogue.meaning: My ear hurts.

dialogue.target: À l’oreille droite ou à l’oreille gauche ?
dialogue.meaning: Your right ear or your left ear?

dialogue.target: À l’oreille gauche. Et j’ai mal à la tête.
dialogue.meaning: My left ear. And I have a headache.

dialogue.target: Vous pouvez montrer où vous avez mal ?
dialogue.meaning: Can you show me where it hurts?

dialogue.target: Oui, ici.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, here.

grammar.title: Optional: avoir mal + à + body part
grammar.explanation: Say j’ai mal, then a location: au bras/au pied/au ventre/au dos (à + le); à la jambe/à la main/à la tête; à l’oreille before a vowel; aux dents (à + les). Use the definite article here rather than mon/ma: j’ai mal au bras. Avoir mal expresses pain; avoir du mal à + infinitive expresses difficulty and is different. This lesson practises describing a location, without diagnosis or treatment advice. Droite/gauche in the dialogue mean right/left; full adjective agreement can wait.

sentenceActivity.hint: Start J’ai mal, then the location with à l’.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Oreille begins with a vowel, so use à l’oreille. The accent in à marks the preposition. Au oreille and à la oreille are not correct forms.

lessons.title: Check compound numbers in prices
lessons.subtitle: Check compound numbers in prices
lessons.outcome: Understand 21, 31, 61, 71, 80, 81 and 91 in whole-euro prices and check an amount.

vocabulary.example: Ce sac coûte vingt et un euros.
vocabulary.note: 21 = 20 + 1. Traditional spelling uses et without surrounding hyphens; vingt-et-un is also valid under the 1990 spelling recommendations.

vocabulary.example: Le total est de trente et un euros.
vocabulary.note: 31 = 30 + 1. Trente-et-un is also a valid spelling. Here un goes with masculine euros.

vocabulary.example: Ce manteau coûte soixante et un euros.
vocabulary.note: 61 = 60 + 1. Soixante-et-un is also a valid spelling.

vocabulary.example: Le prix est de soixante et onze euros.
vocabulary.note: 71 = 60 + 11 in metropolitan French. Keep et before onze. Soixante-et-onze is also valid.

vocabulary.example: Le total est de quatre-vingts euros.
vocabulary.note: Keep s for exactly eighty; no s before another number: quatre-vingt-deux.
81 = 4 × 20 + 1. No et and no s on vingt before un. Contrast exactly 80: quatre-vingts.

vocabulary.example: Le total est de quatre-vingt-onze euros.
vocabulary.note: 91 = 4 × 20 + 11. No et and no s on vingt before onze.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to check the numbers.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; use for checking accuracy.

vocabulary.example: Dix heures demain, c’est bien ça ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Ten o’clock tomorrow, is that right?
vocabulary.note: Use to check information you have just heard.

dialogue.target: Bonjour, ce sac coûte vingt et un euros, c’est bien ça ?
dialogue.meaning: Hello, this bag costs twenty-one euros, is that right?

dialogue.target: Oui. Avec ce tee-shirt, le total est de trente et un euros.
dialogue.meaning: Yes. With this T-shirt, the total is thirty-one euros.

dialogue.target: Et les manteaux : soixante et un ou soixante et onze euros ?
dialogue.meaning: And the coats: sixty-one or seventy-one euros?

dialogue.target: Je vais vérifier. Le manteau bleu coûte soixante et onze euros.
dialogue.meaning: I am going to check. The blue coat costs seventy-one euros.

dialogue.target: Le gris coûte quatre-vingts euros, le noir quatre-vingt-un et le rouge quatre-vingt-onze, c’est bien ça ?
dialogue.meaning: The grey one costs eighty euros, the black one eighty-one and the red one ninety-one, is that right?

dialogue.target: Oui, c’est ça.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, that is right.

grammar.title: Optional: build a number from known parts
grammar.explanation: Use et un in 21, 31 and 61; 71 is soixante et onze. Metropolitan 80 is quatre-vingts; 81 is quatre-vingt-un and 91 is quatre-vingt-onze, with no et and no s on vingt before another number. These are compositional applications of the existing complete basic-number/tens sequence, not a claim that basic numbers were missing. The examples use traditional et spacing; 1990 hyphenated spellings are valid too. All sample prices are fictional whole-euro amounts. Centimes and decimal prices are a later task.

answers: Le total est de trente et un euros.
sentenceActivity.hint: Start Le total est de, then the number, then euros.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Keep et in 31. These fixed sentence pieces use traditional trente et un. Trente-et-un is also valid spelling, explained in the study note, but the fixed pieces do not offer that variant. Euros is plural.

lessons.title: Clarify a payment problem
lessons.subtitle: Clarify a payment problem
lessons.outcome: Ask a bank adviser to help clarify a possible duplicate card charge using an amount, date, statement and receipt.

vocabulary.note: Not the restaurant menu.
This phrase does not establish a right to a refund.
A till receipt; keep it if you may need to return an item. Conditions vary by shop and situation.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to check the numbers.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; use for checking accuracy.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking at my bank statement.
vocabulary.note: Masculine. A record of account transactions; this lesson makes no claim about its format or availability.

vocabulary.example: Je vois deux opérations sur mon relevé bancaire.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I can see two transactions on my bank statement.
vocabulary.note: Feminine. Here an entry or transaction on an account, not a medical operation or a mathematical calculation.

vocabulary.example: J’ai été débité deux fois pour cet achat.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have been charged twice for this purchase.
vocabulary.note: Use débitée for a feminine speaker. Learn j’ai été débité/débitée as a bounded payment formula; full passive grammar is optional. Deux fois means twice.
Masculine. Le montant is the sum of money, not a count of purchases.

dialogue.target: Bonjour, je crois que j’ai été débitée deux fois pour cet achat avec ma carte bancaire.
dialogue.meaning: Hello, I think I have been charged twice for this purchase with my bank card.

dialogue.target: Quel est le montant ? Et à quelle date ?
dialogue.meaning: What is the amount? And on what date?

dialogue.target: Trente et un euros, vendredi. Je vois deux opérations sur mon relevé bancaire.
dialogue.meaning: Thirty-one euros, on Friday. I can see two transactions on my bank statement.

dialogue.target: Vous avez le ticket de caisse ?
dialogue.meaning: Do you have the till receipt?

dialogue.target: Oui, le voici. Vous pouvez vérifier le montant ? Je voudrais aussi un renseignement sur un remboursement.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, here it is. Can you check the amount? I would also like some information about a refund.

dialogue.target: Vous voulez vérifier ces deux opérations, c’est bien ça ?
dialogue.meaning: You want to check these two transactions, is that right?

dialogue.target: Oui, je voudrais comprendre.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I would like to understand.

grammar.title: Optional: describe a problem and ask for clarification
grammar.explanation: Use vous with a bank adviser: vous pouvez vérifier le montant ? Je crois que means I think that and presents the possible duplicate charge as something to check. Two statement lines are observations, not proof of two completed charges. A speaker can say j’ai été débité (masculine) or j’ai été débitée (feminine); learn this as a bounded completed-event formula before full passive grammar. Je voudrais un renseignement sur un remboursement asks for information without asserting entitlement or timing. The dialogue offers language only; no bank procedure, promised outcome or legal rule is taught.

pictureActivity.prompt: Choose the French for “an amount of money”.

sentenceActivity.prompt: Build: “Can you check the amount, please?”
answers: Vous pouvez vérifier le montant s’il vous plaît ?
S’il vous plaît vous pouvez vérifier le montant ?
sentenceActivity.hint: Keep vous pouvez before vérifier, then le montant. The polite phrase can start or end the request.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Vérifier stays in the infinitive after pouvez. Both placements of s’il vous plaît are natural with these pieces. Keep the vous form when addressing staff.

lessons.title: Write a short message to postpone
lessons.subtitle: Write a short message to postpone
lessons.outcome: Write a short polite message explaining an absence, proposing a later appointment and closing appropriately.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will be absent on Thursday.
vocabulary.note: Absente for a woman. Je serai is a useful future form of être.

vocabulary.meaning: a conflicting commitment / something preventing attendance
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Something has come up on Thursday.
vocabulary.note: A polite general explanation without personal details.

vocabulary.meaning: to postpone / move to a later date
vocabulary.example: On peut reporter la promenade à dimanche.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We can postpone the walk until Sunday.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; here change a plan to a later time.
Adjective; the same form for masculine and feminine.

vocabulary.example: Je prends le bus parce qu’il pleut.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am taking the bus because it is raining.
vocabulary.note: Que becomes qu’ before il.

vocabulary.meaning: I am writing to you to
vocabulary.example: Je vous écris pour reporter notre rendez-vous.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am writing to you to postpone our appointment.
vocabulary.note: A polite written opening. Follow pour with an infinitive: pour reporter. Écris is from écrire.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Would it be possible to come on Friday?
vocabulary.note: Learn this as a polite written request with de + infinitive. Full conditional formation can wait; de becomes d’ before a vowel.
A common neutral professional email closing. Put your name after it. A short friendly text to someone you know can use à bientôt instead.

dialogue.target: Bonjour Madame,
dialogue.meaning: Hello Madam,

dialogue.target: Je vous écris pour reporter notre rendez-vous.
dialogue.meaning: I am writing to you to postpone our appointment.

dialogue.target: Je serai absent jeudi parce que je dois travailler.
dialogue.meaning: I will be absent on Thursday because I have to work.

dialogue.target: Serait-il possible de reporter notre rendez-vous à vendredi ?
dialogue.meaning: Would it be possible to postpone our appointment until Friday?

dialogue.target: Je suis disponible à dix heures.
dialogue.meaning: I am available at ten o’clock.

dialogue.target: Merci beaucoup. Cordialement, Alex Martin
dialogue.meaning: Thank you very much. Kind regards, Alex Martin

dialogue.target: Bonjour Alex, vendredi à dix heures, c’est possible. À vendredi !
dialogue.meaning: Hello Alex, Friday at ten o’clock is possible. See you on Friday!

grammar.title: Optional: a clear, polite short message
grammar.explanation: Use a greeting, purpose, short reason, proposed alternative, and closing. Pour and de take an infinitive here: pour reporter; serait-il possible de reporter ? Parce que introduces a complete reason with a verb: parce que je dois travailler. J’ai un empêchement is a more general reason when you do not want to give details. Je serai absent/absente is a useful future formula; je suis disponible stays the same for masculine and feminine. This message uses vous to a teacher and cordialement as a neutral email closing. Reporter moves the appointment later; annuler cancels it. These fixed future/conditional formulas keep an A2 task manageable without requiring full conjugation tables.

pictureActivity.prompt: Choose the French for “kind regards (email closing)”.

sentenceActivity.prompt: Build: “I am available on Friday at ten o’clock.”
answers: Je suis disponible vendredi à dix heures.
Vendredi je suis disponible à dix heures.
sentenceActivity.hint: Keep Je suis disponible together. Vendredi can go before the sentence or before the time.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Use à for a clock time, but no preposition before this particular Friday. Both placements of vendredi work with these pieces. Je suis disponible vendredi dix heures is missing à.
